record.paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Can we avoid long abelian cubes over two letters?

evidence.quote: Can we avoid long abelian cubes over two letters?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abelian cube over an alphabet $A$ is a non-empty word of the form $u_1 u_2 u_3$, where $u_1, u_2, u_3 \in A^*$ are words of equal length and each is a permutation of the letters of the others (equivalently, all three have the same Parikh vector, i.e., the same multiplicity of every letter). Given an integer $m \geq 1$, an abelian cube $u_1 u_2 u_3$ is said to be long (of period at least $m$) if $|u_1| \geq m$.

It is known that abelian cubes cannot be avoided over a binary alphabet $\{0,1\}$: every sufficiently long binary word contains an abelian cube. Decide the following:

Does there exist an integer $m \geq 2$ and an infinite word $w \in \{0,1\}^{\omega}$ such that $w$ contains no factor of the form $u_1 u_2 u_3$ that is an abelian cube with $|u_1| \geq m$? In other words, can long abelian cubes be avoided in an infinite binary word?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of avoiding long abelian cubes over a binary alphabet (e.g., abelian cubes uvw with |u| ≥ 2) is reported as open in the combinatorics on words literature. Related and weaker results are known: k-abelian cubes are avoidable over a binary alphabet for k ≥ 3 (Mercaş–Saarela, improving earlier k ≥ 5 and k ≥ 8 results), but the original question about long (ordinary) abelian cubes on two letters does not appear to have been resolved.

status_evidence.title: 3-Abelian Cubes Are Avoidable on Binary Alphabets
status_evidence.snippet: Previously it has been known that k-abelian cubes are avoidable over a binary alphabet for k ≥ 5. Here it is proved that this holds for k ≥ 3.
status_evidence.claim: Partial/related progress: avoidability of k-abelian cubes on binary alphabet for k ≥ 3, but ordinary long abelian cubes case remains a separate open question.

status_evidence.title: Avoidability of long k-abelian repetitions
status_evidence.snippet: questions about whether long k-abelian squares/cubes are avoidable over binary/ternary alphabets
status_evidence.claim: The status of avoiding long abelian cubes over two letters is discussed as an open question alongside related Mäkelä-style problems.
